text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, continuing a recovery from a two-week decline that has now recouped most of its losses. The bounce follows positive comments from the Trump administration about resolving the Iran conflict "fairly soon," which has eased geopolitical risk premiums that were pressuring oil prices—Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th amid those "Iran hopes," but crude has since stabilized in the $89–$92 range as the market digests whether the peace talk rhetoric will actually materialize.

The stock's gain also comes after it was mentioned as "a call of the day" on November 11th, suggesting renewed investor interest in the energy sector. More broadly, oil majors like ConocoPhillips have faced headwinds from talk of a blue-wave midterm election result and growing renewable energy momentum, but a de-escalation narrative around Iran—a major source of supply uncertainty—can ease concerns about supply disruptions and support crude prices where refiners and producers profit.
